definitions.explanation: One's grandmother or someone else's grandmother.

examples.japanese: おばあさんに{会|あ}いに{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to see my grandmother.

examples.japanese: おばあさんは{料理|りょうり}が{上手|じょうず}だ。
examples.english: My grandmother is good at cooking.

examples.japanese: おばあさんが{公園|こうえん}で{散歩|さんぽ}していた。
examples.english: An elderly woman was taking a walk in the park.

examples.japanese: おばあさんに{手紙|てがみ}を{書|か}いた。
examples.english: I wrote a letter to my grandmother.

examples.japanese: あのおばあさんは{一人|ひとり}で{暮|く}らしている。
おばあさんの{作|つく}る{料理|りょうり}が{好|す}きだ。
おばあさんが{道|みち}に{迷|まよ}っていた。
おばあさんは{優|やさ}しい{人|ひと}だ。
examples.english: My grandmother is a kind person.

examples.japanese: おばあさんに{席|せき}を{譲|ゆず}った。
examples.english: I gave up my seat for the elderly woman.

examples.japanese: おばあさんに{電話|でんわ}した。
おばあさんが{重|おも}い{荷物|にもつ}を{持|も}っていたので、{手伝|てつだ}ってあげた。
examples.english: An elderly woman was carrying heavy luggage, so I helped her.

notes:
おばあさん has two uses: (1) addressing/referring to one's grandmother, and (2) referring to elderly women in general.

GRANDMOTHER TERMS BY FORMALITY:
- {祖母|そぼ}: my grandmother (humble, formal writing/speech)
- おばあさん: grandmother (polite, general reference)
- おばあちゃん: grandma (casual, affectionate)
- ばあちゃん: granny (very casual, intimate)

PATERNAL VS MATERNAL:
- {父方|ちちかた}のおばあさん: paternal grandmother
- {母方|ははかた}のおばあさん: maternal grandmother

IMPORTANT DISTINCTION:
- おばあさん: grandmother / elderly woman (extra あ)
- おばさん: aunt / middle-aged woman (no extra あ)
These are different words! Confusing them can be offensive.

RELATED FAMILY TERMS:
- おじいさん: grandfather / elderly man
- {祖父|そふ}: my grandfather (humble)
- おじいちゃん: grandpa (casual)

USAGE NOTE:
When referring to an unknown elderly woman, おばあさん is polite. Using あのおばあちゃん for a stranger can sound overly familiar.
